ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP (foreign and domestic), FATF watch-list, and sanctions screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Reg. (EU) No. 269/2014 and No. 833/2014 as amended), UK OFSI Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN List, and Cyprus MFA designations; screening must be completed within the 90-day KYC window prior to incorporation; enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs and corporates with opaque structures, requiring documented source of wealth and source of funds; records retained per Art. 61A of Law 188(I)/2007.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry) — e-Registry 'Ariadne' portal at https://efiling.companies.gov.cy/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be filed in Greek and/or Latin (English) characters; Greek names require Latin transliteration; the company name must end with 'LIMITED', 'LTD', 'ΕΤΑΙΡΕΙΑ ΠΕΡΙΟΡΙΣΜΕΝΗΣ ΕΥΘΥΝΗΣ' or its abbreviations 'ΕΠΕ'/'ΛΙΜΙΤΕΔ'; Cyrillic, Chinese, and Arabic names must be officially transliterated into Latin or Greek script for the registry and the notarization bundle.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: cyprus (with Greek or Turkish wording implying state patronage)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, counsel files a formal written re-submission with the Registrar within 14 days of the refusal decision, accompanied by supporting evidence (trademark search results, regulatory support letters from the Central Bank of Cyprus or CySEC for sensitive tokens, and a statutory declaration); a further administrative recourse may be lodged with the Administrative Court within 75 days of final rejection under Article 146 of the Constitution, with a possible interim stay; extension of an approved name reservation is granted only upon pending regulatory approvals, otherwise a fresh application and fee are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted — Companies Law Cap. 113 s.104 mandates a physical registered office address in Cyprus; 'virtual office' arrangements are tolerated only where the registered agent maintains a physical seat and statutory records on site, but they are insufficient to evidence commercial substance for the 12.5% corporate tax regime, EU ATAD/transfer-pricing documentation, or bank onboarding, and may trigger enhanced due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 20-25% cumulative probability of unannounced physical inspection within the first 36 months; approximately 10-15% in year one; risk escalates materially if the company engages in related-party cross-border invoicing, has nominee directors, or lacks local payroll and physical storage/maintenance capability for used heavy machinery.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law, Cap. 113 (Cyprus), as amended; see particularly s.3 (mode of incorporation), s.4 (memorandum of association), s.105 (registered office), and the Companies (Amendment) Laws and EU-related instruments.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCORO), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia, Cyprus
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Private Limited Company and accompanying Memorandum and Articles of Association, submitted with a signed statutory declaration of compliance
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Cypriot private limited company; share capital may be nominal, and no escrow account or deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Law, Cap. 113 be approved and that the subscribers' share subscriptions set out in the register of members are accepted and allotted on the terms stated in the Application for Registration. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at 1, Andreas Avenue, 2001 Lefkosia, Cyprus and that the Registrar be so notified. RESOLVED that [Director 1] be appointed director and that [Secretary] be appointed company secretary. RESOLVED that the director and secretary shall, severally, open bank accounts, sign commercial documents, instruct legal counsel, and file all required statutory returns. FURTHER RESOLVED that all incidental costs and fees incurred in formation are approved and ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Preparation of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, e-Registry (Ariadni) portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online to reserve the proposed private limited company name. Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English or Greek, incorporating the exact name, registered office, share capital, subscriber details, and limited liability clauses. The name must not conflict with any existing Cypriot or EU protected name or trade mark.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and name reservation request
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Full names, nationalities, and residential addresses of subscribers
Corporate identification documents for any corporate subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, file alternative names and a conformed memorandum within 10 working days; the Registry will issue a fresh availability determination without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in Cyprus or notarially attested by a foreign notary with Apostille
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each subscriber must execute the Memorandum and Articles before a notary, who will attest the signatures. Where a subscriber is a body corporate, execution requires a certified extract of its board resolution and a valid certificate of incorporation. The statutory declaration of compliance is then signed by a Cyprus advocate or licensed legal practitioner.
required_dossiers: Final signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statutory declaration of compliance
Notarized board resolution for any corporate subscriber
Passport or valid national ID of individual subscribers
Apostille on foreign execution where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial attestation or supporting exhibits are rejected, cure by re-execution before the notary and resubmit the completed declaration; foreign signatures must be legalized as required by Hague Convention rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Incorporation Application and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCORO), Nicosia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed incorporation application together with the Memorandum, Articles and statutory declaration by physical lodgement or through the DRCORO e-filing system. Pay the government filing fee. The Certificate of Incorporation will be issued once the Registrar is satisfied that the company has complied with the Companies Law.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of a Private Limited Company
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statutory declaration of compliance
Name reservation receipt
Payment reference for state filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a requisition is raised, respond strictly within the stated period by filing corrected documents, amended articles, or evidence of identity; pay any re-filing fee and request expedited release of the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Company Secretary of the newly incorporated company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting after incorporation to ratify the allotment of shares, adopt the registered office address, appoint the director and company secretary, and set bank signatory mandates. File the officers' particulars and registered office details with DRCORO and keep the statutory registers at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting / pro-forma board resolution
Written consents of appointed directors and secretary
Director and secretary identification documents
Registered office address confirmation from the owner or lessor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DRCORO queries officers' particulars, submit a correction notice and original signed consents; ensure filing within the statutory deadline to avoid late filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, EORI and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Taxation, Ministry of Finance; Cyprus Social Insurance Services; Cyprus Customs (EORI system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax and obtain the Cyprus Tax Identification Number through the Tax Department's TIS portal. Register for VAT if taxable supplies exceed the statutory threshold, and voluntarily if required for cross-border trade in used machines. Register for an EORI number with Cyprus Customs to enable import/export customs declarations. If employing staff, register as an employer with the Social Insurance Services.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office address and management details
Description of actual business activity (wholesale of used construction machinery, ISIC 4659)
Bank account details and director identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Department requests clarifications, file an explanatory letter supported by lease agreements, purchase contracts and corporate resolutions; late registration penalties are appealable under the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Premises Approval and Environmental Compliance Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipality (where registered office/storage yard is located); Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business premises license covering the commercial office and any yard or warehouse used for the marketing and storage of used construction crawlers/excavators. Because the company is a wholesale trader and not a manufacturing facility, file a written environmental exemption/confirmation with the Department of Environment where storage of equipment occurs; arrange licensed waste carrier contracts for any waste oil or hydraulic fluid generated during equipment presentation.
required_dossiers: Lease or title document of the commercial premises
Municipal business licence application form
Site plan and intended use statement
Waste management arrangement with a licensed waste carrier
Written environmental exemption/confirmation request to the Department of Environment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or environmental authority requires further assessment, correct the zoning/use classification by evidence of permitted wholesale storage and provide a compliance certificate from a registered waste collector; any zoning refusal may be cured by appealing under the Municipalities Law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — Cyprus does not impose an industrial licence on the wholesale trading and remarketing of used construction machinery; no manufacturing undertaking is involved.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — no industrial/operating permit is needed for the wholesale trade of used excavators and rollers; ordinary commercial business premises licensing applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment, Cyprus
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA under Category III of the EIA Law (L. 127(I)/2018) because the activity is wholesale distribution and is not listed in Annex I or II; a written exemption/confirmation may be requested for storage yards.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or process VOC emissions are generated. Any site drainage must comply with the Water Pollution (Control) Law (L. 106(I)/2002); hydraulic oils and commercial wastes must be handled by licensed waste carriers under the Waste Law (L. 185(I)/2011), with no discharge to ground water or public sewers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any leased office or warehouse yard, a Fire Safety Certificate from the Cyprus Fire Service and Civil Defense clearance is required under the Fire Services Law and Civil Defense Law. If employees are engaged, an occupational safety inspection under the Safety and Health at Work Law (L. 89(I)/1996) and the Factories and Worksites Law (Cap. 134) must be secured. No separate heavy industrial workplace clearance applies because no manufacturing process is operated.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax Department of the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Cyprus (Tmima Forologias); integrated e-portal 'Tax For All' (Ariadne) at https://taxforall.mof.gov.cy with legacy TaxisNet at https://taxisnet.mof.gov.cy; VAT administration by the VAT Commissioner within the same Tax Department; Customs export processing by Cyprus Customs (Ministry of Finance) under the EU Customs Code (Regulation (EU) No 952/2013).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of a Cyprus Ltd, the Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR) automatically notifies the Tax Department through the integrated register, resulting in issuance of the company Tax Identification Code (TIC). For the used-machinery trading company, the standard sequence is: (i) obtain Certificate of Incorporation (HE number) from DRCOR; (ii) confirm or amend the TIC via Tax For All using TFA forms; (iii) file VAT Form 101 (Application for Registration) with the VAT Commissioner once taxable turnover exceeds or is expected within 30 days to exceed EUR 15,600; (iv) for a foreign-incorporated vendor trading through a Cyprus PE, complete TFA1 registration, appoint a Cyprus fiscal representative under VAT Law Art. 54A, and provide certified constitutional documents, board resolution, power of attorney, bank reference, and PE evidence; a non-resident seller with no PE and no Cyprus fixed establishment is generally required to register for VAT from its first taxable supply in Cyprus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Cyprus-resident Ltd subject to 12.5% corporate income tax on worldwide income with unilateral and treaty foreign tax credit relief; territorial scope applies to non-residents limited to Cyprus-source income; no pass-through election is available to a Ltd; standard capital gains taxation on Cyprus real property and certain share disposals; company is outside any special tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cyprus does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections: (i) IP Box regime election (80% qualifying IP income deduction under Income Tax Law Art. 9A); (ii) Notional Interest Deduction election on new equity (Income Tax Law Art. 9B); (iii) Group Relief election for intra-group loss surrender (Income Tax Law Art. 13A); (iv) VAT group registration election (VAT Law Art. 22); (v) second-hand margin scheme election for dealers in used excavators and rollers (VAT Law Art. 35); (vi) partial VAT exemption method election (VAT Law Art. 30); (vii) advance tax ruling application to the Tax Department on hybrid mismatch and export substance documentation, governed by ATAD 2 implementing Law 33(I)/2020.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) implemented under Cyprus Value Added Tax Law 95(I)/2000, as amended, harmonised with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 15,600 of taxable turnover in the preceding 12 months (or anticipated within the next 30 days) for established suppliers; EUR 35,000 distance-selling threshold for suppliers established in other EU member states; voluntarily registrable for persons making only zero-rated exports in order to recover input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping or digital cryptographic invoice requirement applies to domestic B2B invoices in Cyprus. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing operates through the Cyprus Government e-invoice receiving infrastructure (Peppol BIS 3.0) under EU Directive 2014/55/EU. Periodic fiscal clearance obligations include VIES/EC Sales List filings for intra-EU B2B supplies, Intrastat declarations for dispatches and arrivals, and e-filing of VAT returns and recapitulative statements through the Tax For All portal; machine-to-machine API submission is available for large taxpayers but not mandatory for private-sector issuers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% is available under VAT Law Art. 54 where used hydraulic earthmovers and rollers are physically exported from Cyprus to destinations outside the EU, provided the exporter proves removal from the VAT territory within the statutory evidence windows (in practice not exceeding 90 days from the time of supply) and retains the complete export evidence chain. Intra-EU supplies are zero-rated when the customer holds a valid VIES VAT number, the machinery is transported from Cyprus to the other member state, and the supplier files the periodic EC Sales List. For second-hand machinery, the dealer may elect the margin scheme (VAT Law Art. 35), but export zero-rating is generally preferable because it preserves full input VAT recovery on acquisition costs, spare parts, refurbishment, logistics, auction commissions and export-related fees. Offshore services ancillary to machinery export qualify for zero-rating only where the EU place-of-supply and direct-export nexus rules are documentary proven.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration (SAD/EX1) registered and released in the Cyprus Customs electronic system
Bill of Lading (ocean) or CMR International Waybill (road) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical departure from Cyprus
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank credit confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds under SWIFT LC or wire transfer
Commercial invoice with serial numbers, engine hours, tare weights and Incoterms
Sales contract or purchase order identifying the non-EU or EU acquirer and destination
Packing list and container/vehicle loading manifest
Pre-export ownership and registry documentation for the used machines (engine/plate photographs, CE or previous registration records)
EU acquirer VIES number validation printout for intra-Community zero-rated supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Cyprus Customs and the Tax Department audit the entire warehouse-to-destination evidence chain for zero-rated exports. Missing, inconsistent or falsified SAD/EX1, B/L, CMR, remittance or VIES data triggers retrospective reversal of the 0% rate, re-assessment at 19% VAT, denial or recapture of input VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and administrative penalties including per-day non-compliance fines. Fraudulent or sham export structures assessed under the ECJ Kittel standard (Case C-439/04) attract criminal prosecution (imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fines), penalty assessments, clawback of refunds within the full limitation period, and director disqualification procedures under Cypriot company law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Κεντρική Τράπεζα της Κύπρου), functioning as the national competent authority within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full euro convertibility applies for both current and capital account operations. Cyprus abolished its exchange-control regime in 1994, joined the EU in 2004 and adopted the euro from 1 January 2008, leaving no residual approval powers for cross-border settlements, foreign-currency account holding or repatriation of profits. The only material remittance hurdle is domestic statutory withholding on shareholder distributions: 17% on dividends remitted abroad, eliminable at 0% for qualifying EU corporate recipients under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) and reducible to treaty rates for third-country investors. Because the entity's trade is wholesale remarketing of used construction excavators and rollers, commercial receipts and payments may be denominated freely in EUR, USD, GBP, JPY or other convertible currencies, and no Central Bank or Ministry of Finance authorisation is required for any payment direction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or forced repatriation deadline exists under Cypriot law for export proceeds. Used-machinery sale receipts from EU, Middle Eastern, CIS and Asian buyers may remain offshore and in foreign currency indefinitely without Central Bank approval. The applicable obligations are exclusively statistical: the bank, and where the exporter exceeds the relevant threshold, the company itself, files balance-of-payments, Intrastat or Extrastat reports with the Central Bank of Cyprus and the Statistical Service of Cyprus. The company must retain sales invoices, CMRs, Bills of Lading and customs-export documentation to evidence each transaction; these records carry no cash-conversion or monetary-policy requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency EUR/USD/GBP) with integrated treasury and trade-services desk
Operational Account (EUR) plus ancillary import documentary credit and standby LC facility for used-equipment imports
Operational Account (EUR and USD) supporting Swift-based supplier settlements and SEPA corridors
Capital Escrow Account for non-resident equity subscription pending Registrar of Companies filing, paired with an Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as an ancillary settlement rail for low-value EUR/USD payments, FX conversion and same-day SEPA transfers; Low as the primary or sole treasury rail for this used-machinery trading business. Legal constraints: an EMI holding a Cyprus authorisation or an EU/EEA PSD2 passport may lawfully open a remote corporate account and execute MT103-equivalent cross-border credit transfers, but it cannot issue, advise or negotiate documentary letters of credit, cannot operate as an UCP 600 bank, and typically declines clients whose counterparties include high-risk non-EU buyers. Under the Central Bank of Cyprus AML directives and FATF Recommendation 16, the corporate must maintain settlement capacity only with a licensed credit institution or authorised e-money institution; UK-only FCA-authorised EMIs have no post-Brexit passporting right into Cyprus and are therefore suboptimal. The EMI should be confined to a pre-funding corridor and FX conversion while all sanctioned trade flows and LC-documentary operations are routed through the tier-1 licensed banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner where the entity is non-resident-owned and its entire turnover arises from third-country trading; the tier-1 Cypriot banks require an in-person compliance interview in Nicosia or Limassol, with the company's Cyprus registered agent or introducing lawyer present. Remote opening is permitted only as a narrow exception: all signatories must be EEA-resident, a CBC-recognised introducer (licensed lawyer or auditor) must issue a professional attestation, and the bank must accept a notarised video-KYC. For this Medium-Risk-Enhanced excavator trader profile, remote onboarding is rarely granted at initial account opening and is at best considered after a full first-year transaction history has been established.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU corporate counterparties registered in high-risk or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions (e.g., CIS-linked trading vehicles or Middle-East freight consolidators) appearing in the transaction matrix
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening evidence (World-Check or Dow Jones output), passport and constitutional documents of each beneficial owner, 24 months of audited financials and bank reference letters, signed end-user and anti-diversion attestation, customs-broker Bills of Lading confirming the declared machinery class, and board minutes recording the enhanced due diligence call.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purchase price of secondhand excavators not reconcilable with independent auction or market valuation indices, raising source-of-wealth opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor invoices or auction settlement statements, serial-number-level purchase agreements, independent inspection and appraisal certificates from SGS, Bureau Veritas or recognised national inspection bodies, a completed source-of-funds questionnaire addressing the bank's AML officer, and the share register showing subscribed capital to demonstrate permissible funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency wire transfers in round amounts and rapid re-export to third countries suggesting trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full transaction-to-contract mapping with Incoterms 2020 terms, transport invoices (Bill of Lading/CMR), certified margin analysis by the statutory auditor, and a written compliance charter confirming perpetual name screening and weekly transaction monitoring.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of EUR 75 for the first month and EUR 75 for each subsequent month or part thereof, capped at EUR 900; continued non-payment may trigger administrative strike-off or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form HE32) with attached audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties: EUR 20 for delay up to 1 month; EUR 40 for 1–3 months; EUR 60 for 3–6 months; EUR 100 for 6–12 months; EUR 200 for more than 12 months; filing default beyond approximately 6 months also exposes the company to strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Register of Beneficial Owners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (Central Beneficial Ownership Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June, reflecting beneficial owner data as at 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes an offence under the Beneficial Ownership Law; the company and every officer in default may be liable to fines and, in extreme cases, criminal sanctions; the Registrar may also impose restrictive administrative measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is compulsory for all Cyprus private limited companies unless the entity qualifies as a 'small company' exemption by meeting at least two of the following three criteria for two consecutive financial years: (i) balance-sheet total not exceeding EUR 350,000; (ii) net turnover not exceeding EUR 700,000; (iii) average number of employees not exceeding 10. Exemption is unavailable for public-interest entities, subsidiaries forming part of a group required to prepare consolidated accounts, or where shareholders holding at least 10% of the paid-up share capital request an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the European Union; Cyprus has no domestic GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Cyprus company must file an annual confirmation with the Central Beneficial Ownership Register, attesting that the recorded beneficial ownership data is accurate and complete. The confirmation is due on or before 30 June each year and must incorporate any shareholding transfers or changes in ultimate control that occurred up to 31 May. Changes occurring during the year must additionally be reported to the Registrar within 30 days of the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 380–760 (EUR 350–700) per annum for standard registered office and registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,300–3,250 (EUR 1,200–3,000) per annum for a typical non-listed trading entity, depending on transaction volume and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cyprus levies a flat 12.5% headline CIT. Effective incentives: (i) Notional Interest Deduction on new equity capital, capped at 80% of taxable profit; (ii) IP Box regime providing an 80% deduction on qualifying intangible profits (effective rate ~2.5%); (iii) 95% participation exemption on dividends and gains from disposal of outbound shareholdings; (iv) 0% withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest and royalties; (v) exemption of exchange gains and revaluation profits in certain trading structures; (vi) tonnage tax regime available only for qualifying shipping operators, not applicable to used machinery trading.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form TD2004 (Company Income Tax Return) filed exclusively via the Cyprus Tax Department ARIADNI / TAXISnet electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; tax year coincides with the calendar year (1 January to 31 December).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: TD2004 must be submitted within 15 months after the end of the tax year (i.e., by 31 March of the year following the year after the fiscal year-end; for FY2024 the deadline is 31 March 2026). Provisional tax instalments are payable on 31 July and 31 December of the current tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from wholesale trading, resale and remarketing of secondhand hydraulic excavators, earthmovers and rollers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all sales where title and risk pass in Cyprus or to non-resident buyers where the Cyprus entity is the seller. Indirect export proceeds are fully taxable at 12.5% unless treaty sourcing rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct acquisition cost of used machinery, refurbishment parts, freight in, inspection and reconditioning costs directly attributable to units sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border related-party purchases must comply with arm's length pricing; contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation should evidence the margin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Auto-calculated as Box 1 less Box 2; must reconcile to the audited financial statements of the Cyprus LTD.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gross margin must be consistent with the TNMM/CUP benchmark applicable to used heavy machinery wholesalers; unexplained margin erosion attracts audit scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commissions, storage fees, logistics rebates, spare parts sales, scrappage proceeds, foreign exchange gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders with Cyprus permanent establishment must attribute income to the Cyprus PE on an arm's length basis; treaty-resident recipients may exempt non-Cyprus-source ancillary income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rent of warehousing and depots, employee salaries, transport, insurance, marketing, site inspection travel, professional fees and bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses are deductible only if incurred wholly and exclusively for earning Cyprus taxable income; a non-resident PE must allocate allocable overheads, but head-office charges require contemporaneous evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible items (fines, penalties, non-business entertaining, depreciation that exceeds tax capital allowances); deduct tax depreciation, notional interest deduction and prior year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Typical disallowances for machinery traders: private/personal use of vehicles, revaluation provisions, and expenses unsupported by valid VAT-compliant invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual wear-and-tear allowances and investment allowances on warehouses, forklifts, and refurbishment equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only assets used in the Cypriot taxable activity qualify; allowances are claimed on original cost and cannot create or increase a tax loss for assets leased from non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit per audited accounts, adjusted by Box 6/7; cannot be below zero before application of loss relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must ensure the Cyprus PE profit, after deductions, equals the amount that a distinct and separate enterprise would obtain; TP file must be referenced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed by applying the 12.5% flat rate to Box 8 taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is entered only after the 12.5% computation and is capped at the Cyprus tax attributable to the same income under a valid double tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct provisional taxes paid, GESY contributions recoverable, foreign tax credits, and any deductible off-setting tax withheld at source; balance payable or refunded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident payors withholding 0% on outbound dividends need not submit any further declaration; attach Form TF03 Tax Residency Certificate when claiming treaty benefits on foreign taxes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of TD2004: €100 for the first month of delay plus €50 for each subsequent month up to a maximum of €500. Late payment: 5% surcharge on the unpaid tax plus statutory interest computed at 3% above the ECB refinancing rate (approx. 3.85%–4.15% per annum). Failure to maintain proper books and records: summary fines of €500–€1,000. Deliberate non-filing or fraudulent filing escalates to criminal prosecution with fines up to €6,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Cyprus does not impose withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders. This zero-rate applies automatically under domestic law without prior approval; an anti-abuse clawback may apply where the Cyprus company is resident of a 0% tax jurisdiction? No - rather, the General Healthcare System (GESY) 17% levy applies only to Cypriot tax-resident recipients of dividends, not to non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since the domestic statutory withholding rate on dividends is already 0%, non-resident shareholders receive gross dividends with no requirement to file a relief application. Where the Cyprus company is the payer, the payor maintains a simple written payer's declaration. For any foreign source income flowing through the Cyprus LTD, treaty relief is invoked by obtaining a Cyprus Tax Residency Certificate (Form TF03) from the Cyprus Tax Department, submitting the Form TF03 to the source-country payer, and providing a beneficial ownership self-declaration with the underlying transaction documents. Double tax treaty relief is generally granted at source after submission of the TRC; no pre-clearance with the Cypriot authorities is required for outbound payments.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law: 0% withholding tax on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. EU Interest and Royalties Directive: 0% for associated EU-resident companies. Cyprus double tax treaties commonly provide for 0% on royalties and 0%–10% on interest; in all cases the domestic 0% rate prevails. Royalties paid for the use of trademarks, engineering patents, or technical know-how in used machinery trading are tax deductible for the Cyprus company and faced no Cyprus WHT. Interest on shareholder loans or bank debt is likewise repatriated free of Cyprus taxation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Euro (EUR). Full Cyprus Local File is mandatory where the aggregate value of controlled transactions with related parties in a tax year exceeds either (i) EUR 5,000,000 for transactions in tangible goods (e.g., purchase or resale of used excavators), or (ii) EUR 750,000 for transactions in services, royalties, interest or intangible property. A Cyprus Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated annual turnover exceeds EUR 750,000,000. Entities below the thresholds must still complete the transfer-pricing summary declaration attached to the annual tax return and apply the arm's length principle.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cyprus does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code. Instead, economic substance is enforced through the management-and-control rule for tax residency, Section 60 of the Income Tax Law (GAAR) and the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD). A used-heavy-machinery trading vehicle must demonstrate genuine commercial substance in Cyprus: physical warehousing or inspection premises, qualified staff executing purchasing/sales/re-marketing functions, actual negotiation and decision-making protocols, corporate minutes, and local bank accounts used for the core cash cycle. An arrangement found to be a 'letterbox company' used to capture the 12.5% rate without real activity will be disregarded, and profits will be reallocated on an arm's length basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate non-invoicing or under-invoicing of cash and wire-transfer receipts from sales of used excavators and rollers; omission of deposits in the books; use of undisclosed foreign bank accounts; two-sided (shadow) accounting in cross-border dealer networks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the full undeclared tax at 12.5%, plus 5% late-payment surcharge, statutory interest at ECB rate + 3%, and criminal fines up to €6,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years upon conviction for false declarations to the Cyprus Tax Department.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false tax returns are criminally liable jointly with the company; civil courts may order contribution and restitution for the unpaid corporate tax; travel bans and freezing of personal assets are routinely applied in evasion cases involving cross-border wire transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the Cyprus limited company as a transactional 'mailbox' with no real employees, no physical premises, no local procurement or inspection activity, while routing all substantive buying, contracting and risk-taking of used-machinery trades through Cyprus solely for the 12.5% tax rate or to access treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner invokes the GAAR (Section 60 Income Tax Law) to disregard the artificial arrangement and recharacterize the profits to the real beneficiaries; a 10% additional administrative tax penalty applies on the reallocated tax liability, with treaty benefits potentially revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the company is a mere façade, courts will pierce the corporate veil; directors may be personally assessed for the unpaid corporate tax and civil damages; disqualification orders under the Companies Law may prohibit the director from serving on any Cyprus board, without prejudice to criminal sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing of Used Heavy Machinery
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sales of secondhand excavators and rollers to a foreign affiliated trading entity at inflated discounts, extended interest-free payment terms, exclusion of warranty/after-sales costs from the transfer price, or centralizing risks in Cyprus while allocating profits offshore to a low/zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment under Section 33 Income Tax Law: revision of taxable profit to arm's length, imposition of 5% late-payment surcharge, statutory interest, and a 10% GAAR penalty where the mispricing is deliberate; documentation penalties apply for failure to maintain the Local File once thresholds are exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving the mispriced transactions with knowledge are subject to personal surcharge for the additional tax, liability for false declarations, travel bans, and criminal prosecution if the mispricing masks export of capital or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Sanctions Evasion in Trade Finance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large SWIFT wire transfers or LC proceeds from counterparties in sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Russia-linked dealers) without Enhanced Due Diligence; using misdescribed invoices ('metal commodities' for used excavators); layering of sale proceeds through third-country shell accounts; failing to report suspicious transaction reports (STRs) to MOKAS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Cyprus AML Law (L.188(I)/2007 as amended): fines up to €1,000,000 for legal entities; freezing of the company's bank accounts and assets; separate criminal conviction for money laundering carries imprisonment up to 14 years and fines up to €500,000 (or 10% of annual turnover) for the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors as 'responsible persons' are criminally liable even where the corporate body is separately fined; personal prosecution can result in imprisonment up to 14 years, travel bans, confiscation of personal assets, and a permanent prohibition from serving as a director of any Cyprus-licensed or registered company.
